judged_text: In addGuests.handler.ts, attendees are persisted via createMany (~lines 100-104) before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) (line 165), which is not wrapped in try/catch; if the calendar update throws (bad/missing credentials, API error), the client gets a 500 but the guests are already in the DB and no emails were sent, and a retry then hits the uniqueGuests.length === 0 branch (line 80) returning the misleading emails_must_be_unique_valid BAD_REQUEST — leaving the user stuck with guests added, never notified, and the calendar never updated.

record.issue_text: In addGuests.handler.ts, attendees are persisted via createMany (~lines 100-104) before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) (line 165), which is not wrapped in try/catch; if the calendar update throws (bad/missing credentials, API error), the client gets a 500 but the guests are already in the DB and no emails were sent, and a retry then hits the uniqueGuests.length === 0 branch (line 80) returning the misleading emails_must_be_unique_valid BAD_REQUEST — leaving the user stuck with guests added, never notified, and the calendar never updated.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation first persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` without any `try/catch` or transactional rollback. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (e.g., credential/API failure), the request will fail while the DB has already been updated. On retry, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out existing `booking.attendees`, so it can become empty and triggers `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which is misleading and prevents a straightforward retry to complete calendar update/emails. Emails are also only attempted after the calendar update, so they won't be sent in this failure mode.
